uncīnātōrium, uncīnātōriī n.

noun, second declension

Built on uncīnus, a hook (late Latin, Lewis & Short): the tool that drives the little hooks.

Other words

  • cōnsūtōrium, cōnsūtōriī n.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 31

    Built on cōnsuere, to stitch together, Traupman’s verb for stapling.

Examples

  • Hās chartās uncīnātōriō cōnsue.

    Staple these sheets together.composed

See also paper.

SourcesLewis & Short: uncinus · Lewis & Short: consuo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 31.

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 12.
